title: Erik Hoel · The Intrinsic Perspective — 梦不是在整理白天，是在防止你被白天学傻
title_en: Erik Hoel · The Intrinsic Perspective — Dreams aren't filing away your day, they're stopping your day from making you stupid

questions.question: 梦通常很稀疏（几乎读不清字、看不清屏幕），又很荒诞（一个人同时是两个人）。按 Erik Hoel 的「过拟合大脑假说」，这两个特征该怎么理解？
options: 它们是记忆巩固过程溅出的副产品，梦真正的工作是把白天的经历重放归档
它们是情绪处理的伪装，大脑把白天的冲突改头换面，以免睡眠被惊醒打断
它们说明大脑夜间算力不足，只能低分辨率地重演白天，荒诞是重演出错所致
它们正是梦的功能：类似 dropout 与域随机化，防止对日常过拟合
questions.explanation: Hoel 坚持一个梦的理论必须解释梦是什么样子。大脑的训练集是活过的日子，有限、高度相关，又关不掉学习，于是有过拟合风险；梦的稀疏对应随机丢掉信息的 dropout，荒诞对应往数据里掺入不可能输入的域随机化。主流的记忆巩固说恰恰要把梦的内容当成副产品，而且梦里几乎不出现具体记忆，这正是他反对它的理由。
questions.question_en: Dreams are typically sparse (you can almost never read text or a screen) and hallucinatory (one person is two people at once). Under Erik Hoel's overfitted brain hypothesis, how should these features be understood?
options_en: They are by-products spilling out of memory consolidation, whose real job is to replay and file away the day
They disguise emotional processing: the brain reshapes the day's conflicts so you won't be startled awake
They show the brain lacks computing power at night, so it replays the day at low resolution and the oddities are replay errors
They are the point: like dropout and domain randomisation, they stop overfitting to repetitive days
questions.explanation_en: Hoel insists a theory of dreams must explain what dreams are like. The brain's training set is lived experience: limited, highly correlated, and it can't switch learning off, so it risks overfitting. Sparseness corresponds to dropout, randomly discarding information; bizarreness corresponds to domain randomisation, injecting impossible inputs. The mainstream consolidation account has to treat dream content as a by-product, and the near-absence of specific memories in dreams is exactly why he rejects it.

questions.question: Hoel 把小说和电影看作「外包的梦」，却又说「虚构过量的唯一解药是好的虚构」，而不是少看虚构。他这样主张的理由是什么？
options: 艺术与娱乐的高下只是品味与阶层之分，好作品的价值在于带来更多审美愉悦
套路娱乐是副本的副本，自身已过拟合，满足冲动却完不成功能
任何虚构都能起到做梦的作用，所以问题只在总量太多，挑选内容并不重要
虚构会挤占睡眠时间，只有足够精彩的作品才值得用来替代真正的梦
questions.explanation: 既然梦有功能，履行不了功能的梦就是坏的梦。他说娱乐对世界的再现是拉马克式的，副本的副本直到图像糊掉，像糖果仍有热量却不再有营养。所以艺术与娱乐的区分在他这里有机制依据，不是势利眼；禁欲不管用，安全的是审美家而不是苦行僧。
questions.question_en: Hoel treats novels and films as 'outsourced dreams', yet says the cure for too much fiction is good fiction rather than less of it. What is his reason?
options_en: The gap between art and entertainment is just taste and class, and good work matters because it gives more aesthetic pleasure
Formulaic entertainment is itself overfitted: it feeds the urge to dream but can't do the dream's job
Any fiction serves the function of dreaming, so the only problem is quantity and choosing what to watch doesn't matter
Fiction eats into sleep, so only truly great work is worth the trade against real dreaming at night
questions.explanation_en: If dreams have a function, a dream that can't perform it is a bad dream. He calls entertainment Lamarckian in how it represents the world: copies of copies until the image blurs, like candy that still has calories but no nutrition. So for him the art/entertainment distinction has a mechanistic basis rather than being snobbery; abstinence doesn't work, and it's the aesthete, not the ascetic, who is safest.

questions.question: 对于票房被续集垄断、网红脸和汽车外形越来越相像，Hoel 在《我们过拟合的世纪》里给出的解释是什么？
options: 根源在大众口味退化，观众越来越不愿冒险，市场只是被动地迎合这种保守需求
根源在资本垄断与过长的版权期，只要拆分巨头、缩短版权，多样性就会自然恢复
系统高效到反馈极紧、判别器极灵敏时就会过拟合，像模式崩溃那样压缩产出的方差
根源在生成式 AI 的普及，模型训练于同质化数据，又把同质化内容大量回灌给文化
questions.explanation: 他把文化看作一个关不掉学习的宏观大脑：当生产足够高效、反馈足够紧、判别足够灵敏时，就像生成对抗网络中过于挑剔的判别器让生成器只产出相似的东西。版权、垄断、互联网等解释他认为多半有道理，但都只是同一件事的不同层面。他明确说不能怪 AI，这个趋势早于 ChatGPT，AI 只是加速。
questions.question_en: Faced with box offices dominated by sequels and increasingly similar influencer faces and car designs, what explanation does Hoel offer in 'Our Overfitted Century'?
options_en: The root is declining public taste: audiences grow risk-averse and the market merely caters to that conservatism
The root is monopoly capital and overlong copyright, so breaking up giants and shortening terms would restore diversity
Hyper-efficient systems with tight feedback and picky discriminators overfit, collapsing output variety
The root is generative AI: models trained on homogeneous data pump homogeneous content back into the culture
questions.explanation_en: He treats culture as a macroscale brain that can't stop learning: when production is efficient, feedback tight and discrimination sharp, it behaves like a GAN whose overly picky discriminator drives the generator toward near-identical outputs. He grants that explanations like copyright, monopoly and the internet are mostly right, but sees them as layers of the same thing. He explicitly declines to blame AI: the trend predates ChatGPT, and AI only accelerates it.
